title: LitLinker: Supporting the Ideation of Interdisciplinary Contexts with Large Language Models for Teaching Literature in Elementary Schools
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of helping elementary school literature teachers design interdisciplinary contexts for reading instruction. The authors argue that creating such contexts requires substantial search, interpretation, and alignment work across disciplines, which is difficult for teachers to do efficiently and in ways that fit classroom practice.

To support this task, they develop LitLinker, a human-AI collaborative web system powered by the GLM-4 large language model. LitLinker uses multiple LLM-based roles to recommend interdisciplinary contexts, analyze the relationships between contexts and reading materials, support question asking and editing, and generate structured lesson plans with course outlines, introductions, and activity suggestions. The system is grounded in a context database, prompt templates, and iterative design with teachers.

The paper reports two empirical studies in mainland China. Experiment I is a within-subject study with 16 participants, described as novices of Chinese literature teaching / teacher trainees from university programs, who compared LitLinker against a baseline LLM web app while completing lesson-planning tasks using elementary Chinese reading materials. Experiment II consists of expert interviews with elementary Chinese language teachers. Results suggest that LitLinker improves the depth of interdisciplinary integration in lesson plans, reduces workload, and is viewed positively for supporting ideation, although teachers raise concerns about content quality and reliability in purely generated material.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A large language model (LLM)-powered interactive system for generating, analyzing, and organizing interdisciplinary literature-teaching contexts and lesson plans.
identified_tools.use_case: LitLinker was studied as an LLM-powered support tool for elementary Chinese language teachers to ideate interdisciplinary contexts, analyze reading materials, and generate structured lesson plans; the baseline was a generic LLM web application using the same model.

findings.finding_summary: In a within-subjects study (n=16), LitLinker outperformed a baseline LLM web application on outcome lesson-plan quality. Specifically, the paper reports significantly deeper integration of different subjects in the generated lesson plans, and significantly higher satisfaction and efficiency, with reduced task workload.
findings.measure: Lesson plan quality ratings based on Content Alignment, Alignment with Educational Objectives, and Depth of Integration; task workload (NASA-TLX); usability (SUS); creativity support (CSI)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods within-subject study with qualitative follow-up and without reported effect sizes in the provided text. The design is empirical, but the evidence strength is limited relative to a full RCT or meta-analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports statistically significant improvements, but no effect sizes are provided in the excerpt, so the practical magnitude cannot be verified. The impact appears promising but remains unclear from the reported data.
